notes: LOOT THAT FITS THE STAGE: a monster in the wilds drops what a monster of its level would, never more than its region's best - the Mirefen's skeletons no longer drop the mountain's finest blades, and the maze chest there holds a steel axe instead of an obsidian blade
WHO LIVES WHERE: each region's packs now follow its own mix (the Ash Fields are mostly orcs), and the pack nearest the town is orcs, not a nest of imps

ARMOUR SETS, READ RIGHT: a set's line now shows what each tier adds up to (five pieces of Oilskin give +5 DEX, not +3), the Greyhold Warden set guards a little better than the Blackiron that comes before it, and the shop says which stat a weapon hits with

READY FOR OTHER LANGUAGES: every word the game shows - its menus, messages, quests, dialogue, items and story - can now be translated, and Options has a Language row (it follows your system's language unless you pick one). French is on its way
FOOTERS THAT FIT: a screen's row of keys closes up when its words run long, so a wordier language never pushes it off the edge

THE NIGHT OF ASH TEACHES THE GAME: the first night is now a walk through everything a hero needs, one thing at a time. Ash hounds come out of the fire inside the gate - one tells a lunge to roll through; Bram is pinned under a beam on Upper Street; Sela binds your cuts and hands you a leather cap to wear from your pack; you carry water from the well on the green to three burning homes, and each fire dies as you douse it; embers swarm the square for your first skill; and Maren waits at the shrine. Hurt on the way, and the game shows you how to drink a potion
A FIRST NIGHT YOU CAN SKIP: hero creation has a First night toggle (Tab) for players who have walked it before

A DAWN YOU WATCH: when Maren has the letter, the Night of Ash ends on the town itself. The camera drifts from the shrine across Pixelheim as the fires gutter out one by one and the red night greys toward morning; the survivors stand together on the square and speak in their own voices - Maren, the mayor out of his hall, Bram and Sela beside you - and when Fafnyr is named, he roars, and his shadow sweeps over the town. Then the day begins: Pixelheim, day one
E moves the talk on and Esc skips to the morning; with Reduce motion the camera cuts and nothing shakes

PIXELHEIM, REBUILT BY DESIGN: the village is laid out anew on a bend of the river at the mountain's foot. The gate road runs straight to the Town Hall, which faces the square; the inn and Odo's store flank the way in; Maren's shrine stands in a grove under the cliffs; Hilda's forge sits on Forge Lane down to a bridge, with the orchard, the fields and a new barn across it; Vex brews beside her herb garden; the homes keep to Hearth Lane; and the green runs down past the old well to a fishing dock on the bend

THE AGES BUILD ON PLANNED LOTS: new cottages rise by the river walk, the barn across the bridge, lamps along Upper Street and then the gate road, and the fountain at the square's heart. A walled garden hides between the homes and the river - and someone left something in it

ONE PLATE FOR WHAT THE GAME TELLS YOU: the next step, a message and every line of the battle log now sit on the same dark plate, readable over grass and snow alike, with a gold word in front where it helps (Next, Quest accepted, Quest complete, Level up, Mastery)
SHORTER, CLEARER MESSAGES: taking a quest names the task instead of repeating what the giver just said; gold is written as gold everywhere it's told (+60 gold, not +60g); level ups no longer shout

THE KEYS YOU CHOSE: every line that names a key - the Night of Ash's steps, the hints, the journal page among the bones, the festival's ring toss - names the key you bound. The bones' page used to say J, which strikes; it now says the journal's key

KEYS THAT LOOK LIKE KEYS: every key the game shows you - in a screen's footer, under a conversation, in the menu - is drawn as a raised key with a lit edge and a lip, and it dips when you press it. Pairs sit side by side (W S), choices take a slash (I / Esc), and the arrow keys show their arrows

WHAT TO PRESS, WHERE YOU ARE: the "!" over a villager, a chest or a fishing spot is now the key that does it, on the world's own pixels - and it follows your key if you rebind it. On a phone it stays a "!" beside the Use button

BOSSES THAT LAST: Fafnyr and Morvax used to fall in a few seconds, before most of their attacks were ever seen. Now a hero of their level needs about half a minute, long enough for all three phases. Floor guardians and every elite stand up to more blows too
STUNS HAVE LIMITS: a stunned monster no longer casts or uses its tricks, but bosses and elites shake off a second stun for a while after the first - Frost Nova can't hold them in place
MATCHING SUMMONS AND POISONS: the dead Morvax raises stand at his level, and monsters on the mountain's floors poison and burn as hard as their level, not their kind's

ARMOUR TURNS ASIDE A SHARE: armour no longer subtracts a flat amount from each hit, it turns aside a share of it. More armour always helps, each point a little less than the last, and no hero is ever immune - a warrior in Blackiron at the gate takes about a third of a hit, not 1. The stat sheet shows how much of a hit of your level your DEF turns aside

STURDIER CASTERS AND ROGUES: mages, necromancers and rogues grow 6 health a level, and cloth wards better (the Mage Robe, the Traveler's Cloak and the whole Frostweave set). Heroes who levelled before catch up when their save loads. Every hero now takes about 6 to 15 hits from a foe of their own level, at every stage

ROADS ACROSS THE ASH FIELDS: paved roads now run from the mountain path west to Blackiron, east to Greyhold and north up the pass to the Frostgate. The orc and wyvern packs that sat beside them have moved off, and Cinderjaw nests in a scorched hollow away from the Frostgate road
A SAFER MIREFEN AND DEEPWOOD: the Mirefen's mimic pack is gone (its trapped chest waits in the far west, by Grandmother Gulp), and the Deepwood's trolls no longer stand at its gate
ENERGY COMES BACK: out of a fight, every hero's mana or stamina slowly returns - casters can walk to the next fight with their spells

FIX: playing an empty save slot dropped a nameless warrior straight into the world, past hero creation and the Night of Ash. An empty slot now opens hero creation for that slot - Esc goes back to your saves, Begin starts the new hero from the very beginning
New hero (N) on a slot goes through creation too, instead of making a default warrior

SHOPS FOLLOW THE STORY: Hilda's, Vex's and Odo's shelves now fill as you win the relics out in the Reach, not only as you climb the mountain - iron, staves and leather from the start, steel and better rings with each relic
MANA AND CURES FROM DAY ONE: Vex sells mana potions and antidotes from the first morning, and Odo dried meat

A TRADER IN EVERY REGION: Marta the Chandler in Saltmere, Quartermaster Brann at the Blackiron camp, Mabel the Sutler by Greyhold's road, and Gunnar's caravan on the Frostgate pass - each with their own pack and one rare piece

GLOVES, BOOTS AND SHIELDS SHOW: gauntlets colour your hands, boots your feet, and the shield you carry hangs on your off hand - a round buckler, a kite or a tower, in its own colours, in front of you or behind as you turn, put away while you draw a bow or cast

EVERY SET FROM HEAD TO TOE: Saltmere's oilskin with its saltwood buckler, Blackiron's soot plate and black bulwark, the Warden's slate and kite, Frostweave's white with the rime orb glowing at your side
The paper doll and the dock's portrait wear it all too

EVERY HELM AND BODY HAS A LOOK OF ITS OWN: Saltmere's oilskin is tarred sea-green, Blackiron soot-black with ember-hot horns, the Warden Greyhold slate with a cyan plume, Frostweave ice white, the City Plate gold on royal blue, Scaled Mail copper on dragon green, Greymaw's Hood wolf grey - and the cloaks, robes and iron each their own

NOTHING YOU PUT ON IS INVISIBLE ANY MORE: Greymaw's Hood and the City Plate now show, and armour that happened to match your hero's own colours (scaled mail on a red warrior, the mage robe on a cyan mage) has its own look
Paladins in soldier's steel, the mayor, Hilda, Odo, Sela and the goblins and orcs no longer step one frame out of time: their swings, stumbles and falls play the frames they were drawn for

THE WEAPON YOU HOLD IS THE WEAPON YOU SWING: a warrior who picks up a bow draws it, a mage with a war hammer swings it, and a ranger with a staff casts. Bare-handed, every hero keeps their own way of fighting

BLADES IN THEIR OWN COLOURS: Dragonbane swings red, the Obsidian Blade violet, the Blackiron Axe soot-dark, the Warden's Longsword Greyhold steel, Tidecutter sea-green - and bows and staves take their wood and stone too
Mages, clerics and necromancers start with an apprentice staff instead of a rusty sword
PLAY ON YOUR PHONE: on a phone or tablet a thumbstick sits under your left thumb and the hero's buttons under your right - hit, roll, use and your first three skills

MENUS BY TAP: every screen gets a row of buttons on a phone - the arrows, OK and Back - in the room beside the page, so it never covers what you're reading. The dock's Menu and the rows themselves answer a tap too

ANY WAY UP: the game fills a phone's screen held sideways or upright instead of sitting in a letterbox, the dock along the bottom and the pages in the middle. Upright, the art stays big enough to see the hero; sideways reads best, and the game says so once
On a computer nothing changes

THE DEEP HUNT: once Morvax is down, the stair behind his throne goes on into the dark. Depth after depth without end, each harder than the last, with foes from every family - wyverns beside wendigos, iron demons beside cutthroats - and an elite guarding every third depth
Every cleared depth opens a hole into the dark beside the way up: keep going, or climb out. The Undermountain's gate offers the first depth and the next one past your deepest
YOUR DEEPEST DEPTH is kept in your save and shown on the bounty board and in the journal. A new deepest pays its hoard; a depth you've beaten pays only its fights

THE TOWN SENDS YOU OUT: once Maren has asked for the relics, Pixelheim's folk have errands in the Reach - Hilda wants Blackiron ore, Vex wants Saltmere's sea glass, Sela has heard of the smugglers' rum, Bram needs the miners' humming cheese, Ana her father's badge from Greyhold and Mira yeti fur from the Frostgate. They pay in embers, potions, gems and cheese
SIDE QUESTS FOLLOW THE STORY: a hub's side quests wait for its first word - Rook after Wenna's smugglers, Pell after the lost crew, Fenwick once the yard is clear, Gunnar once the wolves are gone
THE JOURNAL IN CHAPTERS: Main (the chapter, its steps, the promises that carry it), Side, Bounties and Story. A/D turns the chapter, W/S scrolls, and every promise says where to go
THE MAP MARKS WHO IS WAITING: villagers with a quest to give or take back show as green squares on the map

THE MOUNTAIN COMES LAST: since the Night of Ash the mountain's gate is barred. Maren knows what opens it - the four relics the five climbers left in the Reach. Win them back from Saltmere, Blackiron, Greyhold and the Frostgate in any order, bring them home, and she opens the gate with the fifth: her promise
THE STORY IN CHAPTERS: Out of the Ashes, The Five Relics, The Ashen Throne, The Deathless. The line above the dock points at the next relic still out there
MAREN REMEMBERS: each relic you win brings her story of its owner - Tam's stew in the snow, the five marks on the black iron, Oskar's shield and Liane's lantern

THE MOUNTAIN, RETUNED: its floors now start around level 12 and end around 18. The Mossy Cellar's slimes are no field slimes any more, every guardian shows its level at the gate, the floors drop the mountain's best loot, and the early hoards are gems, rings and potions worth having
THE REACH GROWS THE TOWN: two relics open the Village age and all four the Town, and the bounty board posts its notices as relics are won
The region chapters' quests and bosses pay half the XP they did, so a hero arrives at each one about its match
Long messages now grow upward instead of running under the dock
A hero from before keeps everything: whoever has cleared a floor finds the gate open, and Maren goes straight to her next ask

THE FROSTGATE PASS: a narrow road climbs north out of the Ash Fields into snow - pines on white ridges, a frozen lake, and at the head of the pass Liane's observatory, built over the old ice cave. Up here the wind blows where the birds would sing
THE HERMIT AND THE CARAVAN: Aske keeps Liane's door fifty years on; Gunnar's caravan is stuck by the road, and Linnea, its herbalist, picks frost lilies for Vex

THE ICE CAVE: down the observatory's stair, yetis, wendigos and frost mammoths in frosted galleries - and Rimefang, a white drake that breathes frost, curled up on Liane's Lantern, the fourth of the five relics
ICE FISHING: stand at the hole cut in the lake's ice, face the water and press E for icefin
THE FROSTWEAVE: hood, robe, mitts, boots and a rime orb (+INT), and the Rime Staff - woven at Vex's cauldron from frost lilies and yeti fur

GREYHOLD: a new road leaves the east edge of the Ash Fields for Oskar's old fort on its hill - breached walls, a stone yard, his statue, and the keep where turncoats in red cloaks have made themselves at home
THE OLD GUARD'S CAMP: Sergeant Ulla, Brother Teo and Fenwick, a turncoat who changed his mind, keep a guardhouse by the road with five quests between them

THE CELLARS: down the keep's stair to the guardroom, the old cells, the crypt and the captain's hall, where Greyhold's dead garrison still stands watch - and the Hollow Captain keeps Oskar's Shield, the third of the five relics
THE GREYHOLD WARDEN: helm, hauberk, gauntlets, boots and a kite shield (+STR and +DEX), and the Warden's Longsword - forged at Hilda's from the fort's old steel
THE BLACKIRON MINES: a new road leaves the west edge of the Ash Fields into a valley of spoil and scrub, with a miners' camp on the road and the shaft mouth in the northern cliff

THE SHAFTS: torchlit galleries of goblin diggers and spearmen, stone golems in the cart hall, ore veins in the dead ends - and the Seam Warden, an iron demon guarding the deep seam. It leaves the Black Ingot, the second of the five relics
MINERS' QUESTS: Foreman Garrick's lost crew and the black seam, Dagny's ore and cart hall, and Old Pell's canary, lost somewhere off the west gallery
THE BLACKIRON PLATE: helm, plate, gauntlets, sabatons and a bulwark (+STR, heavy), and the Blackiron Axe - forged at Hilda's from the seam's ore
The release flows give the camera-smoothness check a second try, so a busy machine no longer fails it
ARMOUR SETS: pieces of one set worn together give more - at three pieces and again at five. The bonus shows on every piece (what you wear of it, what more would give) and on the stats page

THE SALTMERE OILSKIN: hood, coat, gloves, boots and a saltwood buckler, light and quick (+DEX), and the Tidecutter, a sea-glass dagger on a pearl grip. Hilda crafts them from what the coast gives: sea glass, pelts, fish and pearls
Every region still to come brings its own set
The craft guide now knows fishing: it tells you where the fish and pearls a recipe needs come from
SALTMERE'S PEOPLE: Old Wenna, whose brother Tam climbed the mountain fifty years ago and never came back; Harbourmaster Brin; Ola the Fisher; and Rook, the honest kind of smuggler

THE SEA CAVE under the western headland: six torchlit chambers of drowned skeletons, slimes and crabs, two chests - and the Tidecaller in its grotto. It leaves Tam's Ladle, the first of the five relics

QUESTS on the coast: the smugglers' story and the Tidecaller for Wenna, crabs on the jetty and the lighthouse lens for Brin, your first catch for Ola, the smugglers' captain for Rook - and in Pixelheim, Pip's cat wants fresh fish
FISHING: stand at the end of Saltmere's jetty, by the lagoon or on the eastern rocks, face the water and press E. Fish, sea glass, the odd pearl - and the odd boot
NEW FOES from Shade's Mini World: giant crabs, smugglers, gunners, their captain and the slime king

THE REACH GROWS: a new road leaves the bottom of the marsh, down through the cliffs to SALTMERE - dunes and pines, a fishing hamlet on the beach, a lagoon, a jetty out into the sea and a cave under the western headland
THE COAST is wild: slimes, goblin smugglers and drowned skeletons keep their camps on its dunes and beaches, and sea glass washes up to gather - a new crafting material
Saltmere's doors are shut for now: its people, their quests and the sea cave come with the coast's own chapter
Behind the scenes: new ground for the regions to come (Shade's sea in three depths, docks, snow, ice and cobbled stone) and a tool that turns a drawn sketch into a map
CLEAR WARNINGS: a new option in Options paints every boss's and elite's warning mark in gold-and-dark hazard stripes with a heavy outline, so it reads by its pattern whatever colours you see

LARGE READING TEXT: everything you read at length - conversations, the story's captions, the town tour, hints, the quest line, the battle log and messages - in the big type. Long lines grow the window upward instead of running off the screen

HINTS: the first time something hunts you, the game tells you about the dodge roll (with your own key); each new skill says what it does when you learn it; the notice board and the bounty board explain themselves the first time you walk up. Once each, and Hints in Options turns them off
Story captions now wrap instead of running past the edge of the screen

FURNISHED ROOMS: every interior is dressed with Shade's own furniture. The inn has tables on a red rug, a candle by the beds, herbs hanging from the wall and kegs in the corner. Odo's shelves are stocked and his floor is crowded with produce, Hilda hangs her weapons on the wall beside a rack, an armour stand and a grindstone, Vex keeps jars, herbs and a reading desk, and the town hall gathers around a long council table under its banners

YOUR HOUSE TOO: a lamp, hanging herbs, a bread shelf, a chest and a pie table in the hut, a dining corner and kitchen as it grows - and wherever you've set your own furniture, the house makes room for it
THE NIGHT OF ASH: the scavenger on the road now keeps to its meal until you walk up to it or strike, instead of jumping you before you've had a look around
DUSK ON THE SQUARE: as the sun goes down the townsfolk walk to the square and stand about the well, then go home for the night

SHOPS GROW WITH THE TOWN: each new age brings Odo, Hilda and Vex more stock, and a signature item you can only buy in Pixelheim - Lamplighter's Sausages and the Lamplit Blade in the Village, a Fountain Day Roast, the Fountain Guard and a Fountain Tonic in the Town, Banquet Ribs, City Plate and a Phoenix Draught in the City

FESTIVAL DAYS: finish an age and Pixelheim celebrates for a day - confetti, stalls, everyone out on the square, and Barker Jory's ring toss. Land two rings of three for a prize of gold and festival pies

THE WORLD SOUNDS ALIVE: birds by day and crickets by night outdoors, the town chattering once it has folk again, fire crackling by the camps' torches, at Hilda's forge and through the burning village, and wind moaning down the mountain's floors (deeper and lower in the Undermountain)
STORY THEMES: Fafnyr and Morvax each have a theme of their own as they first appear, the dawn after the Night of Ash has one, and each ending has its own before the victory music takes over
NEW SOUNDS: the dodge roll whooshes, a named monster roars when it sees you, and a bounty jingles when it's yours
Every new sound is made in code (godot/tools/synth.py) in the same chiptune voice as the rest
THE THRONE BELOW: when Morvax falls he kneels, and you decide. Destroy him - or, if Maren told you her story of the five and you carry Liane's last page, lay him to rest
TWO ENDINGS: each has its own words at the throne, its own evening in town (a festival with confetti, or five lanterns on the square for the five who climbed) and Maren's own last words

SETTLER ARCS: Iva, Wren, Loras and Mirelle each have two more asks once they live in town, and the last one grows their perk. Iva tops your healing potions up to three, Wren's riders make you a tenth faster above ground, Loras's war-horn lifts his song to +20% crit, and Mirelle's savings grow 3% a day
A settler with something to ask still heals you or plays first, then asks
The town tour's captions now always sit above the dock, however long they run
THE BOUNTY BOARD: a second board on the square, with a wanted poster on it, posts the wilds' named monsters one by one as you clear the mountain's floors

FIVE NAMED MONSTERS: Old Greymaw in the Whispering Forest, the Drowned Knight in the Sunken Marsh, Cinderjaw on the Ash Fields, Mossback in the Deepwood and Grandmother Gulp in the Mirefen. Each is its kind grown huge, keeps to a lair marked on your map, and has its family's trick plus one of its own: a howl that calls wolves, hands from the bog, fire spat three ways, a thrown stone, a leap
THE REWARD: the bounty is paid where it falls, with a piece of gear nothing else drops. Pixelheim talks about it when you get home. A named monster stays dead
THE BATTLE LOG now stands above the quest line and grows upward, so a long fight's lines never run under the dock
DODGE ROLL: Shift (or L, or the right shoulder button) throws you three tiles in a blink - nothing can touch you mid-roll. Rebind it in Options
HITS THAT LAND: a blow you strike freezes the world for an instant and the screen jolts; a blow you take hits harder still, and a boss's harder than that (none of it with Reduce motion)

ELITES HAVE A TRICK: elite wolves and slimes lunge down a marked line, greenskins cleave the ground before them, golems and mimics stamp a ring, imps and wyverns spit firebolts, and the undead raise a guard that turns most of a blow
EVERY TRICK IS TOLD: the ground marks or the monster flashes first - read it, roll out
SOMETHING SPEAKS IN YOUR SLEEP: resting at the inn - or in Sela's tent - now and then brings a dream of the stair below, and a voice that knows your name
THREE DREAMS: the first night after the fire, after the Barrow Crypt and after the Sunken Forge; each comes once, in order
THE STORY UNDER THE MOUNTAIN: three graves in the Barrow Crypt with a fourth name chiselled away, a broken seal on the Sunken Forge's anvil, and Fafnyr's last words about the voice below
LIANE'S JOURNAL: ten pages lie on the floors, one per first clear, telling how five heroes of Pixelheim climbed to renew the Ember Seal fifty years ago - read them in the journal's new Story tab
MAREN REMEMBERS: as you go deeper, Elder Maren tells you about the graves, the seal, and finally the truth about the five
MORVAX KNOWS YOU: the lich greets you by name, and his last words are for someone else
THE QUEST FOLLOWS THE STORY: asking Maren about the graves and telling her what Fafnyr said join the main quest as side steps
A PROPER BEGINNING: a new hero no longer just appears in town. You are a courier carrying a letter to Elder Maren, and you arrive on the road the night Pixelheim burns
PLAY THE NIGHT: drive off a scavenger at the gate, walk into the burning village, pull Bram from under a beam, let Sela bandage you, and give Maren the letter
THE VILLAGE ON FIRE: Shade's own flames and drifting embers burn in the ruins under a red night sky
DAWN: the survivors gather on the square, Maren reads the Crown's answer aloud, and Pixelheim decides to rebuild - with you
HEROES FROM BEFORE: your existing heroes skip the night and carry on where they were
FAFNYR BREATHES FIRE: the dragon sweeps a line of flame at you and rains embers in his later fury - every attack marked on the ground first, so you can step out
MORVAX CALLS THE DEAD: the lich rings himself with death and raises skeletons to his side as he weakens
THREE PHASES EACH: both bosses roar at two thirds and one third of their health, and fight faster every time
THE ENDING SHOWS YOUR TOWN: slay Morvax and you walk home to a festival - the camera shows the Pixelheim you built, age by age, before the credits roll
MORE TO DO IN THE WILDS: Ana, Bram, Mira and Old Tomas have new jobs - orc raiders on the ash road, imps with a cheese knife, grave moss for the looms, walking stones in the Deepwood
LAMPS AT NIGHT: the town's torches stand cold by day and burn after dusk, with a warm glow around each, and the windows light up too
SMOKE FROM THE CHIMNEYS: every finished house has a thread of smoke rising from its roof
A CAT, A DOG AND TWO CHILDREN: Pixelheim has a cat that judges you, a dog that leans on you, and - once it's a village - Pip and Nell running about the square
HOME AFTER DARK: villagers, builders, the children and the animals go home at night and are back in the morning (never vanishing while you watch)
THE TOWN TALKS: the villagers bring up your latest deed first - the floor you came back from, the boss you felled, the project you paid for, the settler who moved in
EVERY RECRUIT A STORY: the folk waiting in the wilds now each give you a small quest in the journal - help them, and they come home to Pixelheim
A LUTE AND A VAULT: Loras wants his lute back from a Deepwood troll, and Mirelle wants two gems for her vault's first shelf - no more paying them to move
THE LEDGER KNOWS ITS PEOPLE: the projects ledger lists who lives in town and what each brings - Iva's healing, Wren's post, Loras's song, Mirelle's bank
THEY NOTICE THE TOWN: settlers say new things as Pixelheim becomes a village, a town and a city
FIX: every map but the town logged an error as it was built since v0.90 (the props and door signs of other maps failed to build); the release checks now fail on any script error
PLOTS YOU CAN SEE: the next age's houses and the fountain are staked out where they'll stand, a log fence and a crate of materials on each
BUILDERS WAITING: a builder stands by every plot - talk to them and they'll tell you what it is and exactly what it still needs
THE TOWN RISES: fund a project and the camera shows you what went up the moment you're back in town - and says so when Pixelheim becomes a village, a town or a city
COMING HOME: walk back into town after Fafnyr or Morvax and Pixelheim lets you know it noticed
PIXELHEIM BURNS: a new story now ends with Fafnyr setting the village alight - and a new hero starts in what's left of it
THE ASHES: the store, the forge, the brewery, the inn and the homes are charred frames with smoke still rising; only the stone hall stood
TRADE ON THE SQUARE: Odo, Hilda and Vex sell from stalls on the square until their roofs are back, and Hilda and Vex craft there too; Sela keeps a tent for anyone who needs a bed
REBUILD IT: the Hamlet is four projects on the board - Odo's store, Hilda's forge, Vex's brewery, and the inn with the homes - each one cheap, and each one opens its doors again
THE SURVIVORS SPEAK: Elder Maren and Mayor Aldric remember the fire, and the town's first age now reads as rebuilt, not spared
YOUR VILLAGE IS SAFE: a hero from before keeps every roof they had
VILLAGE PROJECTS: the town's charters are gone - each age of Pixelheim is now a handful of projects you fund one by one, with gold and a material from the wilds
THE TOWN CHANGES AT ONCE: street lamps, market stalls, cottages, the fountain, a slate hall, the grand avenue and flower beds each appear the moment you fund them
PRICED FOR A HERO: the Village costs 800g in all, the Town 2200g, the City 2700g - instead of 2500g, 7000g and 15000g
EARNED, NOT BOUGHT: the Village opens once the Ruined Watchtower is cleared and a settler has come home, the Town once Fafnyr is slain, the City once Morvax is cast down
A BOARD ON THE SQUARE: a notice board by the square lists what Pixelheim needs; Mayor Aldric now talks before he opens his books
YOUR TOWN IS SAFE: a hero from before keeps every project their town had reached
THE STORY KNOWS: bringing a settler home, lighting the streets and setting Fafnyr's scale in the fountain join the main quest - as side steps, never in the mountain's way
A STORY TO FOLLOW: Pixelheim now has a main quest in three chapters - Under the Mountain, The Ashen Throne and The Deathless - from Sela's first job to Morvax's throne
ALWAYS KNOW WHAT'S NEXT: a quiet line above the dock names your next step, and steps aside in fights and menus
THE JOURNAL LEADS WITH IT: your chapter, your next step and a word of advice come first, then the promises you've made
ASK THE ELDER: Elder Maren and Mayor Aldric now end every conversation with what you should do next
RUN AHEAD IF YOU LIKE: a hero who goes deeper early is never sent back for an errand
PATCHES TO PICK: herbs, reeds, ember shards, deep roots and grave moss grow in patches around each wild region - walk over one to gather it, and it grows back after a while
SOMETHING ON EVERY FLOOR: each dungeon floor hides one patch too, of rarer stuff the deeper you go
GATHERING TEACHES FORAGING: every patch you pick trains it, and a better forager often picks two
A FIRST BREW: Vex's quest now asks you to brew your first health potion at her cauldron
A SHIELD OF REEDS: Hilda has a job for you too - weave a Reedwoven Buckler at her forge, and keep it
MONSTERS CARRY WHAT YOU NEED: dire wolves drop a pelt half the time, imps a horn about a third of the time, and Fafnyr leaves a scale every time he falls
WOLVES IN THE WOODS: a wolf pack now lives in the Whispering Forest and another in the Sunken Marsh
A FIRST JOB AT THE FORGE: the Reedwoven Buckler takes 3 marsh reeds at Smithing 1, the Iron Helm opens at Smithing 2, and Scaled Mail needs one dragon scale, not two
WHERE TO FIND IT: a recipe you can't make yet says where each missing material comes from, in the pack's Craft tab and at Hilda's and Vex's counters
YOUR TRADES IN VIEW: the Craft tab shows your Smithing and Alchemy levels and XP, and a craft that levels a trade says so
FIX: the Wolfstooth Collar, brewed at the cauldron, now teaches alchemy instead of smithing
CAMPS IN THE WILDS: every pack lives by its own camp - a tent in its land's colours and a torch burning beside it - so you can see where trouble waits before it sees you
THE MIMIC GIVES ITSELF AWAY: its chest shudders for a moment before it bursts out beside you, already hunting
